question.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,0)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{14}\sqrt{x}, & \,1\le x\le 4 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=0]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,0)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|0}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{7}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=0] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{14}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{3}{14}{x}^{5/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{49}{x}^{7/2}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{49}(128-1) \\  & =\frac{381}{49}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=0] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=0]-{\mu }_{X|0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{381}{49}-{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{7})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{381}{49}-\frac{3}{49} \\  & =\frac{378}{49} \\  & =\frac{54}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
